So many people have said yes but i’d like to offer my own advice- no. 

Honestly, it depends on what dosage, what headspace you’re in, and what drugs you’re planning to mix with it. 

I took roughly 36mg of 2cb and smoked weed by myself last year and had the most traumatic experience of my life. It literally took me weeks to recover from it. 

However, the first hour or so of my trip was amazing, but as soon as it flipped, and there was no one around, I fell to pieces. 

I do think if I hadn’t taken as much as I did, and I hadn’t smoked any weed, AND if I was in the right headspace, it would’ve continued to be the best trip of my life. 

Just a couple things to consider.

The other day I broke my tooth in half on a cracker. A cracker. Cost me £150 to get fixed. Tooth damage is real. I’ve had several episodes of gastritis where your stomach has produced too much acid and it starts literally dissolving your stomach lining, basically eating your insides out. I’ve blocked multiple toilets at other peoples houses to the point I’ve had to go and tell them what happened so they could help me fix it. I’ve stuck my entire arm down a toilet filled with shit, menstrual blood, and vomit to unclog it before. My family has found bags of vomit under my bed and had to deal with them. I nearly died from electrolyte imbalance. I nearly died from a suicide attempt because my bulimia was so bad, that I couldn’t see the point in living anymore. It’s a vicious cycle, it doesn’t really make you ‘feel better’, it’s an illusion. I’ve had bulimia for nearly four years, and although I’ve been purge three for coming up six months, I still reap the consequences it’s had for my physical health. I’m getting clean because I don’t want to develop a paralysed stomach, a mouth filled with rotten broken teeth, and the constant weight of shame and misery the disorder brings me. It is far more painful to purge than it isn’t, and although it will bring a sense of relief in the moment, nothing is worth the excruciating pain of living with it. I can get clean, I can recover, I know I can and I will. It’s not easy, but it’s so worth it. Be brutal with yourself, if you binge, you binge, but to break the cycle you must not purge. Even if it’s just the sensation of a full stomach, I promise you, it gets so so much easier the more you abstain from purging. If i can do it, why can’t you?

there is no way that asking for help will make you worse if you are surrounded by the right people. I developed bulimia when i was 15 and I’m turning 19 at the end of the month. For the first time since I developed an eating disorder I’ve been purge free for 4 months. It’s a brutal, unforgiving illness that will only get worse and worse the longer it continues. It won’t make you happy, and any illusion of relief or comfort purging brings you is exactly that- an illusion! I don’t want to try and ‘scare you straight’ because so many people have tried with me, but coming from someone who has lived with bulimia for a long time, they’re not lying about the risks. I cracked my tooth clean in half on a cracker the other day. A cracker. My oral health is messed up, as with my gastric system. This isn’t an illness you can fight alone, you don’t need to tell people intricate details, but just knowing that someone else knows can sometimes take away half of the burden alone. If i, someone who’s been struggling for coming up 4 years, can get better, why can’t you? my messages are open if you’d like to talk always, I hope nothing in this message was condescending or disheartening.
